93b410fce3ec: feat(takeoffs): **see how the wind flows over a takeoff, in 3D.** Every takeoff page has a new **Wind flow** section: a clean relief model of the site and its surroundings from our terrain data, a dial for the wind direction and a slider for its strength. 5666394f2444: perf(i18n): **pages load less text.** Each page now sends your browser only the interface text it actually shows, instead of every translation in the app. The Docs pages carry about 60% less, and pages such as your profile about 85% less, which helps most on slow mobile connections at the foot of a hill.
038b886f20a0: fix(flights): **your original IGC files are never changed any more.** Correcting a flight's wing or date, renaming a wing, or importing from Logfly with a different wing name used to rewrite the stored IGC file to match. Now the correction is saved in your logbook only, and the file stays exactly as your instrument recorded it, so a downloaded IGC is always the genuine one you would submit to a league or a competition. Uploading the same flight again keeps the file already stored.
f7f66b9d0dea: feat(flights): **a better-looking, easier-to-read 3D view of your thermals.** The single-thermal 3D view and the new shared-thermal view now use We-Fly's own colours on a warm background (deep charcoal in dark mode), with distance fog for depth. The thermal is a soft glowing column that widens and narrows with your turns, with its core as a bright line and bubbles rising at the pace of the climb. Your track is solid where the replay has been and faint ahead, its shadow sits on the ground grid, a dashed line drops from you to the ground, and an altitude scale stands beside the climb, so height and position read at a glance. Climb-rate colours match the 2D thermal map. The view eases in when it opens, unless you have asked your device for reduced motion.
95182e0cce8e: feat(admin): **server health follows the move from Apache to nginx.** The web server check on the Server health page now reads nginx's status page and flags dropped connections, with requests per second and open connections alongside. It still recognises Apache, so nothing goes dark while the server switches over. The public round-trip and certificate checks are unchanged.
80701882b772: feat(flights): **the Wind tab uses your Vector Vario's measured wind when it has one.** On flights logged with a Vector Vario, wind direction, speed, altitude bands and the speed × altitude heatmap now come from the instrument's second-by-second wind readings instead of being estimated from thermal drift, so you also get wind for glides and flights with few thermals. A **Measured by Vector Vario** badge next to the confidence pill tells you which source you are looking at. Flights from other instruments keep the thermal-drift estimate as before.
f3e6e4a8fa32: feat(email): **a more useful welcome reminder when your logbook is still empty.** The reminder now leads with the fastest route for XCTrack and Air³ pilots: set up FolderSync once, with your server address and username already filled in, and every flight lands in We-Fly on its own. It also lists the other ways in: moving over from XContest, Syride, SeeYou or Logfly, Flyskyhy, Google Drive, or a plain upload. It now arrives exactly a week after you sign up, and reads well on a phone.
3ae90a6f208e: fix(takeoffs): **save the 3D print and replay video files on an iPhone home-screen install.** When We-Fly is added to the home screen of an iPhone or iPad, **Download STL** and the replay video export now open the share sheet, where **Save to Files** keeps the file and leaves you in the app, instead of a preview with no way back.
09fde2b72fe6: fix(security): **connecting autorouter always brings you back to We-Fly.** A crafted link to the autorouter connect button could send you to another website once the connection finished, which a phishing page could abuse. The return address is now checked strictly, and the new PGPilot connection uses the same check.
da2c95ddcb02: fix(xc-planner): **the planner starts on today's date and says why you cannot continue yet.** Pilots got stuck on a greyed-out **Continue** button because no flight date was picked, with no explanation on a phone, where there is no hover to show a tooltip. The flight date now starts on today (change it any time in the **Design** step), and a short note above **Continue** says what is still missing. From the **Airspaces** step on, the date and launch time you are checking stay on the map next to **Back** and lead the panel header, so you always know which day the airspaces, NOTAMs and briefing are for; tap the date to go back and change it. Once you move on to checking airspaces, that date is saved in the page link, so a plan you share or reopen the next day still shows the day it was checked for.
1fe619dad310: fix(replay): **the Reach button stops spinning when you press Play.** In the flight replay and the comparison replay, pressing Play or turning Reach off while the reachable ground was still being worked out could leave the button spinning for the rest of the replay. It now stops, and turning Reach on before the 3D view has finished loading draws the area as soon as the view is ready.
76801239dccb: fix(brand): **the pilot dot on the app icon and the browser tab too.** The icon on your home screen, the browser tab icon, the bookmark icon and the We-Fly profile picture used a simplified logo without the dot under the wing, which stands for the pilot. They now show it, like the rest of the app.
95eae98fe8b4: fix(map): **maps recover on their own instead of breaking after a glitch.** On a phone, the **XC planner** map could still get into a state where every tap threw an error, even after last month's fix. The map now notices this before handling a tap, jumps back to its last good view and keeps working, and an odd tap that carries no position is simply ignored.
ad204a13dea7: fix(security): **fair-use limits work again on every server.** A library update this morning made our request limiter speak a dialect our database does not understand, so every limited page (takeoffs, community, uploads) quietly fell back to a simpler per-server counter and filled our error log. The limiter now talks to our database again, so the limits are shared across the whole app as before and nothing changes for normal use.
7a850c9e9425: fix(observability): **fewer false alarms behind the scenes, so real problems get fixed faster.** When the free weather service behind a flight's **Weather** tab is briefly down, We-Fly no longer files it as a bug on our side (the tab still says the weather is unavailable and works again once the service is back), and cancelling a search in the ⌘K search box by typing on is no longer reported as an error. When the weather service sends back a garbled answer, the tab now says the weather is unavailable instead of failing. And when you upload a flight over terrain We-Fly has not mapped yet, a dropped connection while it fetches the elevation data is retried once, so your flight is less likely to end up without its ground heights.
d8b0a98b1176: fix(upload): **your IGC file is kept exactly as your instrument wrote it, accents included.** Some instruments write the pilot name, the site or other header text in an older character set (a "Jérôme" or a "Clécy" saved as Latin-1). We-Fly used to convert those letters on upload, so the file you downloaded again was no longer the one you recorded, which can break a signed file you submit to a league. Uploads from the **Upload** page, connected apps and instruments, Flyskyhy and other Leonardo-compatible apps, the WebDAV folder and **Google Drive** import now store the original file byte for byte.
d3adcd1ac384: fix(flights): **sorting your logbook and the community flights is right across all your flights.** In the **Logbook** and **Community** > **Flights**, sorting by a column now always orders all matching flights before the next ones load: flights with no value for that column (no G-force data, no duration, no glider name) come last in both directions instead of opening the list, wing and site names sort without caring about capitals, and sorting by **Launch type**, **Track speed** or **Scoring speed**, which used to fall back to the date, now works.
87ba7c6d9a69: fix(brand): **the pilot is back in the logo.** The dot under the wing, which stands for the pilot, was missing from the logo in the header, the footer, the sign-in page and shared club pages, because those spots used the simplified small version. The app now always shows the full logo with its pilot, a touch larger so the name reads as before. Only the browser tab and the home screen icon keep the simplified version, where the dot would be too small to see.
3d1e9ca2d400: fix(badges): **the Thermal Strength badge matches the max climb on your flight.** The badge now reads the same max climb your flight page, logbook and cockpit show, held over 5 seconds, instead of a one-second spike that a gust or a GPS jump could inflate. The tiers stay at 3, 5, 7 and 10 m/s. Badges you still meet keep their place, and a tier your flights no longer reach is removed without any notification.
959343589241: fix(flights): **re-uploading an older flight no longer stores it twice, and cleaning up keeps your original.** Flights uploaded before May 2026 were no longer recognised when you uploaded the same file again, so the logbook got a second copy. We-Fly now recognises the file from its GPS points whatever version analysed it first, and updates your flight instead of copying it. Copies already stored show on your **Anomalies** page as **Duplicate copy**; **Resolve all** now deletes the newer copy and keeps the original flight with your wing name, notes and annotations (it used to pick the shorter flight, and two copies of one file are the same length).
016cc6bf8b8e: fix(flights): **flights that cross midnight UTC get the right date and the right low saves, and re-uploading a tow flight keeps it a tow flight.** When your logger started before 00:00 UTC and you took off after it (an afternoon flight in the Americas), the flight landed on the day before; it now lands on the day you flew. On flights still in the air after midnight UTC, low saves and the speed-bar analysis were matched against the wrong minutes; they now line up with your thermals. Re-uploading a flight you had marked **Towed** or **Powered** reset it to a foot launch and counted the tow as a thermal again; your choice is now kept. A file whose date is missing or impossible (a logger that wrote `000000` before its first GPS fix) is no longer stored with an invalid date. Glide averages on the **Phases** tab now weigh each glide by its length, so a 15 second glide no longer counts as much as a 20 minute one.
0efd69adc914: fix(flights): **your altitude curve no longer dips under the ground on low sites, and flatland tows keep their real height gain.** Loggers record barometric altitude against standard pressure (1013 hPa), so on a high-pressure day a field near sea level reads below zero: under a 1030 hPa high, a winch field at 30 m shows about -110 m. We-Fly took that for a broken sensor and swapped to GPS altitude every time the reading crossed zero, which cut height gain (a tow from 30 m to 400 m counted 250 m instead of 370 m), added fake climbs and sinks of more than 20 m/s, and dropped seconds of track. A reading below zero is now treated as valid. On the flight's altitude chart, the **Baro** curve is now set to the terrain at takeoff, like setting your vario before launch, so it lines up with the GPS and ground curves; the label says **set to takeoff**, the baro maximum in the flight summary uses the same correction, and a tap on the new **ⓘ** next to the **Baro / GPS** switch tells you the shift applied to that flight. A new help article, **Why Baro and GPS Altitudes Differ**, explains standard pressure, high and low days, and which altitude to trust. Your IGC file is not changed.
c0a07dada016: fix(comparison): **the map style picker is reachable again in flight comparison.** On the **Carte** view of a same-day comparison, the menu button in the top-right corner covered the switch for the map background, so you could not change it. The switch now sits just below the toolbar, whatever the size of your screen and whether the stats panel is open.
95fc6575deda: fix(flights): **max gain now counts only height you actually climbed.** It used to be the gap between the highest and lowest point of the track, in any order, so a flight down from a high takeoff showed the whole descent as gain: a sled ride from 2,000 m to a 500 m landing read 1,500 m without a single climb. Max gain is now the biggest climb from a low point to a later high point, so a flight that never climbs shows 0 m. Every stored flight is recomputed, which corrects the logbook column, the community **Greatest Altitude Gain** record and the height-gain badges: a badge that was only earned on descent is removed.
6cb1b57ae6d8: fix(units): **the logbook, flight pages and takeoffs open again on older browsers.** On Firefox 115 (the last version for Windows 7 and 8.1) and Safari before 15.4, every page that shows a distance, speed or altitude crashed with an error. Numbers now display on those browsers too, and a value that rounds to zero still never shows as "-0.0".
6ffcc8333b78: fix(flights): **a single bad timestamp in your file no longer turns a short flight into a 14-hour one.** Some instruments occasionally write one point with a wrong clock in the middle of a flight. We-Fly used to take that point at face value, so the flight seemed to last until midnight and the rest of the track disappeared. That point is now set aside: the flight keeps its real duration, landing place and full track.
67c702ac7dde: fix(community): **the clubs list loads again for every club.** On the **Clubs** page, a club whose pilots had logged a lot of flights could stop the whole list from loading. The totals are now added up as they are read, so even the busiest clubs show their flights, distance and airtime.
b2cb7c7543ef: fix(map): **maps no longer freeze after an odd zoom.** In the **XC planner** and on the other maps, a zoom the map could not work out (for example framing a route while the map was folded away, or a pinch with both fingers on the same spot) could leave it stuck, with every later move throwing an error. The map now ignores such a zoom and keeps its last good view.
0d6da72f7c4e: fix(xc-planner): **meteograms near the edge of a national weather model stay quiet.** When you open a meteogram just outside the area a national high-resolution model covers, the forecast already fell back to the best free model for the spot; that expected miss is no longer reported as an error.
5db4b5c4aae6: fix(xc-planner): **the vertical cut and the airspace list now match the airspace details.** The planner used to work out the zones along your route from a copy of openAIP that can be a few weeks old, while the details you open on a zone come straight from openAIP. A temporary zone openAIP has since removed, like a ZRT after its exercise, could still show up in the vertical cut and then open with "no matching airspace in openAIP". The vertical cut and the **Airspaces** step now read openAIP directly, refreshed daily, so every band you click opens its details, and zones picked from the list keep their whole outline. If openAIP can't be reached, the planner falls back to the map's copy as before.
130aef253080: fix(takeoffs): **takeoffs added from your flights now show on the map.** When a flight launched from a spot we did not know yet, the takeoff we created for it stayed off the **Takeoffs** map, the XC planner and its launch forecast even once it had a name (Marcourt sud, for example), and was only reachable from its own page. Around a thousand takeoffs are back everywhere, and new ones show up straight away. Spots seen only at the start of a drive stay private.
578dbf97cd0a: fix(xc-planner): **the Select button is back in the airspace list.** When you click the map where several airspaces stack up, a long airspace name (such as "LOWER CTA BRUSSELS MINUS LUXEMBOURG…") pushed **Select**, **Show** and the info button off the edge of the window, so you could not add the airspace to your briefing. Long names are now shortened, the buttons always stay in view, and on a phone they sit on their own line under the name.
9200e97424cb: fix(upload): **a log recorded without flying now gets a clear answer.** Uploading a track that never left the ground, such as an instrument test at home, used to fail with "Server error, try again later", which no retry could fix. We-Fly now tells you straight away that the file has no usable GPS points.
f64cc7252ea0: fix(observability): **no more error reports when your connection drops in Firefox.** A page that stopped loading because the network dropped ("Error in input stream" in Firefox) is no longer reported to us as a We-Fly bug, the same as in the other browsers.
0124f00972b1: fix(observability): **fewer false alarms from your browser.** Errors thrown by scripts that the browser itself adds to a page, such as the crypto wallet built into Brave or the in-app browser of Facebook and Instagram on Android, are no longer reported as We-Fly errors. Nothing changes for you, but the real problems you run into reach us faster.
f47d2702e0a9: fix(i18n): **the French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish pages open again.** If you had picked a language, opening a page in it (for example we-fly.cloud/fr) ended with "too many redirects" instead of the page. Every translated public page now loads normally.
82653c73519f: fix(home): **signed in, the home page takes you straight to your logbook.** The big button on the home page still offered to sign you in with a passkey when you were already signed in. It now reads "Go to your logbook" and opens your flights.
1e889d57e616: fix(i18n): **the controls above a flight, the docs and the planner speak your language in full.** The share button and the hints on the flight page's tab bar, and the matching controls above the docs and the XC planner, could fall back to raw text codes because that bar did not receive the page's translations. They now read in your language like the rest of the page.
e6adf9f6e2c6: chore(deps): **steadier forms and screens under the hood.** A newer code checker flagged screens that updated themselves in a roundabout way. Dialogs (edit name, takeoff, airspace, annotation, flight date) now reset cleanly each time they open, editing a takeoff no longer risks wiping what you typed when the page refreshes in the background, and the sign-in, upload, thermal, replay and planner screens do less redundant re-rendering.
4817a398aad5: fix(i18n): **clock times and file sizes in your language.** The time readouts on the altitude, speed and climb charts, the segment stats and the map now follow your language while staying on a 24-hour clock, and the video export writes file sizes the way your language does (4,3 Mo in French). A stricter check now stops new English text from slipping into the app.
1efbe02163ca: fix(i18n): **flight types, dates and calendars follow your language.** The flight type in your logbook, on the flight page and in its summary now reads in your language instead of English or a title-cased guess. Calendars show months and weekdays in your language, date ranges and the time zone in the 3D replay and video export are written your way, the video export shows altitude in your own unit, and the flight page title, link previews and the season recap heading are translated.
7a8bccf98ce1: fix(i18n): **airspace and NOTAM labels follow your language.** Airspace types and classes (Restricted, Danger, Prohibited, Class D), the type and activity in the airspace details, NOTAM subjects such as "Danger area" or "Parachute jumping", NOTAM zone names in the 3D review, the airspace alert in the 3D replay and the START and GOAL pills of the 3D planner review no longer fall back to English. Airspace names from the map data stay as published.
51a63f6466a3: fix(i18n): **community labels no longer slip back into English.** The weekday names and flight types on the community stats charts, the most common type, the records and leaderboards, the following feed, clubs, challenges, Place to be, instrument statistics, the flight search map and the season recap now show their weekday, flight type and placeholder names (Anonymous, Unknown takeoff, Other) in your language instead of English.
16e88c1baccf: fix(i18n): **errors in the planner, the uploads and your profile now speak your language.** Messages that came back from the server in English now follow the language you picked: why an IGC file was refused (upload and same-day comparison), why a task file, code or XContest cloud code could not be imported, saving, publishing and deleting routes, tasks and waypoint collections in the XC planner (including the prompt to sign in), Logfly import problems, and the profile sharing link. A takeoff without a name in your shared flights and replays is also translated.
000eeac0d6cb: fix(i18n): **error messages and consent pages follow your language.** Toasts about shared flight and replay links, airspace files, review requests, email preferences and failed requests, the OAuth authorization and device pages with their permission lists, and the confirm or remove page that safety contacts open from an email, were showing English whatever language you picked. They now speak yours.
89ad4f09cc7f: fix(profile): **flight types on your profile speak your language.** The flights-by-type breakdown on your profile, your statistics and pilot profiles showed the scorer's English names whatever language you picked. They are now translated, like everywhere else. Flights the scorer could not classify are counted as Free Flight in those breakdowns and in your data export, instead of a technical free_flight label.
a08605631162: fix(export): **the total distance in your data export is right.** The README inside the archive you download from your profile showed your total distance in kilometres, but the number was really in metres, so 1,250 km read as 1,250,000 km. It now shows real kilometres, and a new section lists the unit of every number in the JSON file (metres for the track distance, kilometres for the scored distance, seconds for durations).
5a8d4e060cc9: fix(i18n): **the last English corners now follow your language.** The notifications menu, the light and dark mode switch, the share menu, the error page, the rate-limit notice, close buttons and date pickers, the Pioneer badge, the 3D thermal legend, the takeoff edit, delete and rename dialogs, the page that explains how to **move your flights to We-Fly**, and the screen where you let an app or a flight instrument access your account were still in English. They are now ready for French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish.
b6e56c2816b4: fix(cockpit): **the Median G-factor card really shows a median.** It showed the single highest value among your filtered flights, so one rough day set the number for the whole season. It is now the median across those flights, worked out the same way as the circling-time and circle-radius cards beside it, and written with your language's decimal separator.
840cdfdd3976: fix(takeoffs): **flight types on takeoff pages keep igc-xc-score's names.** The flight type shown in a takeoff's statistics and recent flights is now exactly the one the scorer gives (Free Flight, Free Triangle, FAI Triangle, Closed Free Triangle, Closed FAI Triangle), translated into your language, each with its own colour dot. A leftover label that called flat triangles "Closed FAI" could never match the stored type and is gone.
2efc4d611e15: fix(i18n): **numbers are written the way your language writes them.** Distances, speeds, climb rates, altitudes, scores and percentages now use your language's decimal comma and thousands separator (7,8 km and 1 850 m in French, 1.850 m in German) everywhere in the app, while still following your unit settings. English stays exactly as before. Dates and counts no longer depend on your browser's settings, which could make some pages flicker as they loaded.
d45ca2ac57c2: fix(badges): **every badge you earn now shows up in your notifications and the badge catalog.** When the team adjusts a badge's steps (say, a Thermal Power badge at 4 m/s instead of the default tiers), badges earned on those steps went missing from the notification bell, the catalog listed the default steps instead of the ones you can actually earn, and the community season recap left them out of its badge counts. All three now follow the steps in force.
8407a009850b: fix(flights): **re-analysing your flights no longer loses your low saves and bar use, or turns a tow into a thermal.** When We-Fly re-runs its flight analysis after an improvement, towed and powered launches keep the launch climb out of your thermals, the driving at either end of a track is trimmed as on upload, and the low saves and speed-bar figures are kept instead of coming back empty. Re-analysed flights now match a fresh upload.
c4dbedc3cb15: fix(layout): **long pages no longer slide the whole app up while you scroll.** On long pages such as an expanded wing on the **Wings** page, scrolling could move the entire app, top bar included, up out of the window and leave an empty band at the bottom. Hidden screen-reader labels were stretching the page behind the app; they now stay inside it, so only the content scrolls and the top bar stays put.
c90a0f4c14e2: fix(observability): **errors from Brave and Firefox on iPhone no longer count as We-Fly bugs.** Those browsers add their own helper scripts to every page, and when one of them trips up, it used to be reported as if We-Fly had crashed. Those reports are now ignored, so real problems stand out in our error tracking.
7b5c2d744fdb: fix(maps): **no more crash when you leave a map right after zooming.** Switching base layer or leaving a page with a vector map (such as the Community map) during the short settle after a zoom no longer throws an error.
c222e9a3633a: fix(nav): **one browser's quirk can no longer take down every page.** The About dialog's release notes now load only when you open it, so a browser that cannot run that part (seen on Chrome 138) loses the About dialog instead of the whole app, and every page starts with less code to load.
3dfbb967f2a1: fix(xc-planner): **Skyways seasons load again.** Picking Spring, Summer or Autumn asked thermal.kk7.ch for datasets it does not have, so the overlay went blank. The seasons now use kk7's own names, Winter joins the list, and a season saved in your browser under the old names falls back to All year instead of a blank map.
d1ab3810e4e4: fix(admin): **server health says why Apache workers are not monitored when the status page is redirected.** If Apache answers the local status probe with a redirect (typically the HTTP→HTTPS rule on the port-80 site), the check now names the redirect and where it points, instead of suggesting to enable `mod_status` again, and the server-health doc gives the small Apache site that fixes it.
c8156bc5d2e2: fix(xc-planner): **the Skyways Layer, Season and Time pickers open again.** In the XC planner's Map layers panel (and the Layers menu on flight maps), these lists were opening behind the panel, so clicking them seemed to do nothing. They now open on top.
bc6d79671025: fix(api): **highest and lowest altitude are back in flight data.** The community wing statistics averaged every wing's highest altitude as 0 m, and `GET /api/v1/flights/{id}` sent partner apps neither the highest nor the lowest altitude of a flight, because both read a field name the flights are not stored under. Both now read the stored figures.
9b7b40236ac8: fix(auth): **stay signed in between flying days.** We-Fly used to sign you out after 24 hours without opening the app, so most pilots had to log in again on every visit. You now stay signed in for 30 days of inactivity (a full re-login is asked every 90 days), and a brief database hiccup no longer signs everyone out. Deleting your account or resetting your password still ends every session immediately.
cbd71d32d3dc: fix(auth): **resetting your password now signs out every other device for good.** An old copy of your session, say on a phone you lost, could get itself signed back in after a password reset, and could even add another Google, Facebook or GitHub login to your account. Now a reset or an account deletion ends every other session at its next request, and a social login only joins your account when it uses your account's email. Admins who impersonate a pilot are signed out too if their own sessions are revoked or their admin role is removed.
eaa2f723ff6c: docs(privacy): **the Data Retention Policy and the Privacy Policy now say how long you really stay signed in.** The retention policy still said sessions end after 7 days, and the privacy policy only called the sign-in cookie "session-based". Both now give the real rules: 30 days after your last visit, 90 days at most, and straight away when you sign out, reset your password or delete your account.
0c38ca9fe94f: fix(deps): **math in the guides now renders with the patched KaTeX.** The math plugins carried their own outdated copy of KaTeX with a known security flaw; they now share the app's up-to-date one, which also keeps the formulas' HTML and styles from the same version. Two build tools were updated to their patched releases too.
df2289582b18: fix(admin): **the MongoDB log size check explains why it shows n/a.** On the server the MongoDB log folder is closed to the app user, so the check could not read it and only said n/a. Its hint now names the cause and the one-line fix (`sudo chmod 0755 /var/log/mongodb`, which reveals file names and sizes only, never the log contents), and the setup guide says the same.
f961bd53bd9d: fix(flights): **downloading the IGC file from a flight's Summary tab no longer fires failed requests in the background.** The file name link tried to preload the download as if it were a page, which the server refused. It is now a plain download link. We also silenced a chart sizing warning removed leftover debug messages from the upload page, and stopped every page from preloading the public site footer's styles it never uses, so the browser console stays clean when something real needs looking at.
aa25b1168419: fix(flights): **the map marker follows the altitude chart inside a zoomed stretch.** After selecting part of your flight, hovering the altitude chart under the map put the pilot marker (and the readout above the chart) near takeoff instead of at the moment under your cursor. It now lands on the right spot of the stretch you are looking at.
90baa4a4c65b: fix(flights): **your logbook shows your hours and distance again.** The line above your flights reads, for example, "25 of 96 flights · 142h 30m · 3210 km". The hours and kilometres add up every flight that matches your filters, not only the ones loaded on screen, so they are right without scrolling to the bottom. Change a filter and they follow.
9bb144de9287: fix(flights): **old flights no longer lose their G-force chart, sketch, preview image or recap trace when a cached track file is missing.** These now rebuild the track from your original IGC file on the spot, like the flight map already did. The JSON track download recovers the same way.
3cb7d1603351: fix(email): **the welcome reminder for pilots with an empty logbook actually goes out now.** A date mix-up meant nobody ever qualified for it. It also no longer gets lost on a hiccup. If our mail provider refuses the message, the reminder is now tried again on the next run instead of being silently dropped, and every failure is reported to our error monitoring without your email address in the logs.
12c788f0e704: fix(auth): **signing in with Google, Facebook or GitHub no longer leaves you stuck on the consent page.** If you had signed up with a password but never clicked the verification link, then signed in with a social account using the same email, pressing **Accept** on the consent page did nothing. Signing in with the social account now counts as verifying your email, so the consent step goes through and you land in your logbook. Because that password was never confirmed as yours, it is removed, and from then on you sign in with your social account or a passkey. This also stops anyone who registered your email address with a password of their own from getting into your account.
7532a4179ba1: feat(release): **some releases now arrive with sparkles.** Now and then a release is marked as a shiny one. The first time you open We-Fly after it lands, the usual "new version" window is replaced by a holographic card floating in a night sky full of sparkles, with the same links to the release notes and the latest blog post. Move your mouse over it to watch the foil catch the light, tap the glider for an extra burst, and press **Let's fly** to send it off. Shiny releases also carry a **Shiny** tag in the changelog on the About page. If your device asks for reduced motion, the card stays shiny but nothing moves.
303bad457734: feat(airspace): **attach a competition's airspace file to your flight.** When organisers change the official airspace or add buffers for a task, open a flight's **⋯** menu and choose **Attach airspace file** to upload their OpenAir file (up to 8 MB). If another pilot already attached a file to a flight on the same task, We-Fly offers it as soon as you link the task, so nobody has to hunt for it. Files are shared with everyone and stored once, compressed. A comparison uses your own flight's file first, otherwise one of the other pilots' files.
11f3be8d64b0: feat(admin): **see how flights are spread across pilots.** The user management page can now sort users by their number of flights, and a new **Flights per User** card shows how many accounts actually fly, the median and p90 flight counts, the busiest logbook, and what share of all flights the top 10% of pilots upload.
db6b027ddcdc: feat(api): **partner apps can now download your original IGC files.** A new `GET /api/v1/flights/{id}/igc` endpoint returns the file exactly as you uploaded it, for apps you have connected with the "Read your flights" permission, and only for your own flights. Together with incremental sync and upload, this lets a flight instrument keep its logbook and your We-Fly logbook in step in both directions, without ever creating duplicates.
2d343433f1f8: feat(api): **your tasks, waypoints and routes can now sync with your flight instrument too.** Connected apps can download any task, waypoint collection or XC planner route as a `.wpt`, `.cup` or `.gpx` file, and a task exported as `.cup` carries its turnpoint radii and goal line. The "Read/Add your tasks and waypoints" permissions now say they cover routes as well.
02ccbf1559a1: feat(xc-planner): **get an XContest cloud code for routes as well as tasks, right in the briefing.** The last step of the XC planner now has an **XContest cloud code** block next to the file download and QR code. It works for a competition task and for a route, which XCTrack loads as a plain sequence of turnpoints. A task's code is still saved with the task; a route's code is kept only while the planner is open.
d10482e9d6df: feat(xc-planner): **see takeoffs and landings while you plan.** Two new switches under **Map layers → Points of interest** draw every known takeoff (green) and landing field (orange) on the planner map. Hover a point for its name, elevation and orientation. The layer is built to stay smooth: it loads only the part of the map you are looking at once you zoom in, draws thousands of sites in one go, and remembers what it already loaded, so panning back or switching it off and on again is instant.
d363b7a63911: feat(xc-planner): **share a public route in one click, credited to you.** Every public route in **My routes** and **Discover** now has a share button that copies its link straight to your clipboard, without loading the route first; a check mark and a "copied" message confirm it. Only saved public routes can be shared: the **Share** button stays off until your route is saved as public. Whoever opens the link sees who created the route, in the sidebar and on the map, and can save their own copy.
8d61e7e883ae: feat(xc-planner): **add notes to your saved routes and tasks.** A new notes box under the name in **Save & share** lets you write what other pilots should know: best season, conditions, landing options, safety points. Once the route or task is public, anyone who opens it from a share link or **Discover** reads your notes next to your name, in the sidebar and in the summary on the map, and the Discover lists show a one-line preview. Notes stay private while the route or task is private, and keep up to 2,000 characters.
326e82ee1966: feat(xc-planner): **shared routes and tasks now get a map preview card.** Paste the link to a public route or task in WhatsApp, Facebook, Slack or anywhere else that shows link previews, and it unfolds into a card with the route or task drawn on a small map, its name, who made it, the distance, the shape or ruleset, and the start of your notes. Tasks show every cylinder, colour-coded like in the planner, with the optimised line through them. Private routes and tasks keep the generic planner card, so nothing about them leaks through a preview.
cf5823654fc5: feat(community): **search community flights on a map.** The new **Community → Search flights** page is a big map of every takeoff the community has flown from, loaded as you move around. Hover a trace to see who flew it, when, how far and on what wing. 50aafa31c05f: feat(community): **the pilots you follow, right on the Community page.** The **Latest flights** card now opens with a row of the pilots you follow, most recent flyer first. 69c4fb696d1e: feat(community): **a clearer Following page.** **Community → Following** now shows the pilots you follow on the left, most recent flyer first, with a ring on anyone who flew this week. On the right, their flights are grouped by day, each with a small drawing of the track, its distance, duration and max altitude. When several pilots you follow flew the same takeoff on the same day, a line says so. More flights load on their own as you scroll. A few suggested pilots sit under your list, and if you follow nobody yet, the page opens with pilots to follow instead of an empty box. On a phone, the pilots become a row of avatars above the flights.
b7e5b37dee3d: feat(takeoffs): **show only the takeoffs you can fly right now.** A new **Flyable now** switch in the takeoffs filters keeps only the sites where the current wind suits the takeoff orientation, the same check behind the green badge on each card. It works on the list, the map and your favorites, and We-Fly remembers your choice. Sites whose weather is still loading are left out until we know, and on the map the filter kicks in once you zoom in close enough to see the weather.
afe64ffe622d: feat(admin): **an email when a partner asks for API access.** Registering an OAuth application now emails the We-Fly admins with the app's details, requested permissions and a link to review it, so new requests no longer sit unnoticed in the admin panel.
7c8a6ce645ec: feat(community): **the community flights list only shows the mini map when you ask for it.** Like your logbook, the list now has a small trace icon at the start of each row. Hover it to preview the flight on a map. Moving the mouse across the rows no longer pops up a map every time, so the list is calmer to browse. On a phone, where there is no hover, each flight card has a **Preview** button that opens the map right inside the card, just like in your logbook.
412df92cf39c: chore(deps): **flight tables moved to TanStack Table v9.** Your logbook and the flights list on pilot profiles now run on the new major version of the table library. Nothing changes for you: sorting, showing or hiding columns, selecting flights for bulk edits and the trace preview work as before.
f6b3d301dc23: feat(replay): **a calmer, roomier 3D replay, the same for one flight and for the Same day comparison.** The scene now gets the space: playback sits in a solid bar under the 3D view instead of floating over it, with launch, landing, best-climb and biggest-gap markers on the timeline and speeds from 1× to 100×. The height captions over every thermal in the comparison are gone.
0b9b2eaff76e: feat(nav): **links stay inside We-Fly, and outside links say so.** Links to We-Fly pages (docs, flights, profiles, the privacy policy) now open in the same window, so the installed app on your phone no longer throws you into the browser; Back brings you to where you were. 4c1f273eeabe: feat(nav): **a lighter way around We-Fly, without the left sidebar.** The top bar now holds the four places you go: **My flying** (Logbook, Cockpit, Success), **Community**, **Takeoffs** and **XC planner**, plus **Admin** for admins. 6d93ad7e45fb: feat(filters): **filters open in place, and search finds your flights and takeoffs.** On a computer, **Filters** now drops down a wide panel under the bar instead of covering the page: presets, flight, location, time and performance (now including a **minimum distance**) side by side, with a calendar that dots the days you flew, the matching flight count, and **Done**. The search box now sits in the top bar (**⌘K**) and finds takeoffs, your flights, pilots, pages and actions such as applying a saved preset; with nothing typed it shows your recent flights. f76bc541f3c4: feat(nav): **a clear way back instead of breadcrumbs.** The old breadcrumb trail above pages is gone. Signed in, the documentation now opens inside We-Fly with a quiet section menu, **← category** on each article, and Docs / What's new tabs on the home page.
c970e2333c2c: feat(xc-planner): **the XC planner and the docs join the new look.** Signed in, the XC planner now opens inside We-Fly like any other page: the three steps (Design, Airspaces, Briefing) sit in the bar under the top menu, your route settings in a panel on the left, and the distance card and **Continue** button on the map. Takeoff pages drop the breadcrumb, since Takeoffs stays highlighted in the top bar.
d4a1fc31044a: feat(design): **every page now wears the new look.** Logbook, Cockpit and its views, Success, each flight's tabs, Community, Takeoffs, Profile, Developer and Admin share the same calm style: a clear title with a one-line summary, a row of key numbers, framed panels and quieter tables. On the Logbook and Cockpit, a filter row under the title shows each active filter as a pill you can remove, your saved presets, and how many flights match. On a flight, the tabs (Summary, 3D Replay, Phases and the rest) move up into the bar beside a back arrow to the Logbook. Nothing was taken away: every chart, table, button and setting is still there.
671723a6a8f3: feat(community): **pick flights straight from the map on your phone.** On **Community → Search flights**, tap anywhere on the traces and every flight passing under your finger shows up in a small card over the map, so overlapping traces are no longer a guessing game. dc1b5f9e4b91: fix(community): **flight stats fit on small phones.** On the community flights list, the distance, duration, quality and route efficiency under each flight card no longer wrap or squeeze on narrow screens: they sit in two tidy rows on the smallest phones and in one spaced-out row everywhere else.
17fb450fa77e: fix(replay): **the 3D replay fits your phone.** On a phone the 3D settings now slide up as a sheet instead of covering the whole map, and the camera, share and settings buttons sit in two tidy rows. cc931edb1fd3: fix(nav): **you can see when there are more tabs.** Rows of tabs that don't fit the screen (a flight's tabs, Cockpit views, Admin, the pilots you follow on Community…) now fade out at the edge where more is hidden, and open scrolled to the tab you are on. f92e09955e72: fix(community): **map search is easier to read on a phone, and only shows real flights.** On a phone the flight details under the map now scroll normally. Flights under 5 km of XC distance are left out of the results, along with flights flagged as driving or powered, so the map shows proper flights; a link to a shorter flight still opens.
8aa3cae8a394: fix(cockpit): **the Cockpit map no longer hides behind the bottom menu on a phone.** On a phone the map is now sized to end just above the bottom menu, so you see all of it without scrolling.
3d181c84309d: fix(design): **About, the docs header and the public pages fit a phone.** The About window no longer runs off the right edge of the screen. 8a419d0db8a1: fix(flights): **flight time now counts only the time you spend in the air.** An instrument left running before takeoff or after landing kept adding that time to the flight, because GPS drift made it look like it was still moving: one flight left on overnight showed 13h30 instead of 2h30. 059452e4daf3: fix(community): **the ring around pilots you follow is no longer cut off.** Hovering a pilot in the row of people you follow on the Community page clipped the top of their avatar ring. dbdde3a76bae: fix(community): **unknown wings no longer top the recap.** Flights logged without a wing ("NKN", "Unknown (not in IGC)" and similar) were counted as a wing of their own in **Most popular wings**. They are now left out of the wing rankings and counts.
be2355364351: fix(community): **every takeoff in the recap is readable and clickable.** Long takeoff names in **Epic days** were cut off and now show in full, on phones too. Takeoff names across the recap panels now open the takeoff page.
